coupling: The first edited commit adds a public d8 test fixture that creates an indexed interceptor supporting IterableToList; with the original runtime scanner it is benign. The second edited commit copies the prototype property list into a vector and scans it in name/details pairs; without the new fixture the path is not reachable from JavaScript. Together, Array.from selects the fast interceptor path, the paired scan walks past the vector boundary, and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow. Each edited commit alone leaves the probe clean.
